info.title: Numeric range to regex in Node.js script

diffs.patch:
Index: package.json
===================================================================
--- package.json	
+++ package.json	
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+{
+  "name": "range-to-regex",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "description": "Convert a numeric range such as 1-100 into a single regular expression that matches any number in that range.",
+  "type": "module",
+  "main": "index.js",
+  "bin": {
+    "range-to-regex": "cli.js"
+  },
+  "files": [
+    "index.js",
+    "cli.js"
+  ],
+  "scripts": {
+    "start": "node cli.js",
+    "test": "node --test"
+  },
+  "engines": {
+    "node": ">=18"
+  },
+  "keywords": [
+    "regex",
+    "regexp",
+    "range",
+    "numbers",
+    "numeric-range"
+  ],
+  "license": "MIT"
+}

parts.text:
Project set up and verified. `1-100` → `^(?:[1-9]\d?|100)$`.

Files:
- `package.json` — ESM project, `npm test` uses Node's built-in runner, `range-to-regex` bin
- `index.js:170` — `rangeToRegex(min, max, { anchor })`, plus `parseRange` and `matches`
- `cli.js` — `node cli.js 1-100` (prints the pattern; `--no-anchor` optional)
- `test/index.test.js` — brute-force checks every range `0..100` against values `0..130`

No dependencies needed. Run `npm test`.
